In 2005, he made his film debut with a minor role in The Constant Gardener directed by Fernando Meirelles. In the same year, he appeared as 'Barman' in the television movie Transit.       "title": "80's & 90's Authors",

      "document_sha256": "dba8c853fef3fc3a56776bd0ab903ba6f15ed7e49f1fd2e936fb3d11506cc4e7",
      "window_ref": "w_177da5523f166cc0b3a3aa11",
      "text": "---\ntitle: 80's & 90's Authors\ndate: 2025-01-01\n---\nStephen Edwin King was born on September 21, 1947, at the Maine General Hospital in Portland. His parents were Nellie Ruth (Pillsbury), who worked as a caregiver at a mental institute, and Donald Edwin King, a merchant seaman. His father was born under the surname \"Pollock,\" but used the last name \"King,\" under which Stephen was born. He has an older brother, David. The Kings were a typical family until one night, when Donald said he was stepping out for cigarettes and was never heard from again. Ruth took over raising the family with help from relatives. They traveled throughout many states over several years, finally moving back to Durham, Maine, in 1958.\n\nStephen began his actual writing career in January of 1959, when David and Stephen decided to publish their own local newspaper named \"Dave's Rag\". David bought a mimeograph machine, and they put together a paper they sold for five cents an issue. Stephen attended Lisbon High School, in Lisbon, in 1962. Collaborating with his best friend Chris Chesley in 1963, they published a collection of 18 short stories called \"People, Places, and Things--Volume I\". King's stories included \"Hotel at the End of the Road\", \"I've Got to Get Away!\", \"The Dimension Warp\", \"The Thing at the Bottom of the Well\", \"The Stranger\", \"I'm Falling\", \"The Cursed Expedition\", and \"The Other Side of the Fog.\" A year later, King's amateur press, Triad and Gaslight Books, published a two-part book titled \"The Star Invaders\".\n",
      "offset": 0,

      "text": "---\ntitle: Peter Gatien, the '90s 'club king,' wants his final say\nauthor: The New York Times\ndate: 2020-04-04\n---\nNEW YORK — \"Thoughts flash in your mind of incredible nights here, whether it was Jay-Z, or Junior Vasquez, or the thousands of people inside and outside, waiting in line,\" said Peter Gatien, the nightclub impresario who lorded over the 1990s club scene in New York City.\n\nIt was a brisk Wednesday in early March, a few days before the city shut down because of the new coronavirus, and Gatien was at La Colombe, a cafe inside the brick warehouse that once housed the Tunnel, the massive nightclub on West 27th Street that is now celebrated as a crucible of hip-hop.\n\n\"Just the raw energy, the exuberance,\" he said, sipping an iced tea. \"You don't see it anymore.\"\n\nTimes change. The Tunnel, a former warehouse where Biggie Smalls and Busta Rhymes once barked out raps to frenzied throngs, is converting to offices and luxury retail, blending seamlessly with the gleaming Hudson Yards to the north.\n\nAnd Gatien, with his icy demeanor and swashbuckler eye patch, is no longer the \"King of Clubs,\" as he was hailed by The New York Post in his '90s heyday. His spectacle megaclubs in the city — Limelight, Palladium, Club USA and the Tunnel — were raking in more than $1 million a week at the time, he said, before a drug trial, which he ultimately won, cost him, well, basically, everything.\n",

Kennedy and urges him to issue a second Emancipation Proclamation to eliminate racial segregation. |\n\n|\n\n16 December |\n\nKing, Ralph Abernathy, Albany Movement president William G. Anderson, and other protesters are arrested by Laurie Pritchett during a campaign in Albany, Georgia. |\n\n|\n\n1962 |\n\n||\n\n27 July-10 August |\n\nKing is arrested at an Albany, Georgia prayer vigil and jailed.       "window_ref": "w_c245563b7cf525db4038a447",
      "text": "At the beginning, the show had 28 affiliates, but eventually rose to over 500. King occasionally entertained the audience by telling amusing stories from his youth or early broadcasting career.\n\nWishing to reduce his workload, King began hosting a shorter, daytime version of the show in 1993. Jim Bohannon, King's primary fill-in host, took over the late night time slot. After 16 years on Mutual, King decided to retire from the program. The final broadcast of The Larry King Show was heard on May 27, 1994; Mutual gave King's afternoon slot to David Brenner and Mutual's affiliates were given the option of carrying the audio of King's new CNN evening television program. After Westwood One dissolved Mutual in 1999, the radio simulcast of the CNN show continued until December 31, 2009.\n\nLarry King Live\n\nLarry King Live began on CNN in June 1985. King hosted a broad range of guests, from figures such as UFO conspiracy theorists and alleged psychics,One notable guest was Sylvia Browne, who in 2005 told the Newsweek magazine that King, a believer in the paranormal, asks her to do private psychic readings. to prominent politicians and entertainment industry figures, often giving their first or only interview on breaking news stories on his show. After broadcasting his CNN show from 9 to 10 p.m., King then traveled to the studios of the Mutual Broadcasting System to do his radio show, when both shows still aired.\n\nTwo of his best-remembered interviews involved political figures. In 1992, billionaire Ross Perot announced his presidential bid on the show. In 1993, a debate between Al Gore and Perot became CNN's most-watched segment until 2015.\n",

He wrote or edited over 30 books on New Zealand topics, including the best-selling Penguin History of New Zealand, which was the most popular New Zealand book of 2004.\\n\\nLife\\n\\nKing was born in Wellington, one of four children to Eleanor and Lewis King, and grew up at Paremata. His Glasgow-born father was an advertising executive who had left New Zealand to serve as a naval officer in World War II and had risen to the rank of lieutenant-commander. King's family moved to Auckland for a while, where he attended Sacred Heart College, then returned to Wellington, where he attended St Patrick's College, Silverstream in Upper Hutt. He studied history at Victoria University of Wellington, working part-time for the Evening Post, and graduated with a BA in 1967. \", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1476, \"text_tokens\": 384, In 2016, he appeared in the thriller film The CEO where he played the role of 'Jomo'. \", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1299, \"text_tokens\": 366, \"title_tokens\": 6, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.4395018517971039}, {\"docid\": \"7927\", \"url\": \"https://www.imdb.com/list/ls072153898/\", \"title\": \"80's & 90's Authors\", \"title_span\": [11, 30], \"document_sha256\": \"dba8c853fef3fc3a56776bd0ab903ba6f15ed7e49f1fd2e936fb3d11506cc4e7\", \"window_ref\": \"w_177da5523f166cc0b3a3aa11\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: 80's & 90's Authors\\ndate: 2025-01-01\\n---\\nStephen Edwin King was born on September 21, 1947, at the Maine General Hospital in Portland. His parents were Nellie Ruth (Pillsbury), who worked as a caregiver at a mental institute, and Donald Edwin King, a merchant seaman. His father was born under the surname \\\"Pollock,\\\" but used the last name \\\"King,\\\" under which Stephen was born. He has an older brother, David. The Kings were a typical family until one night, when Donald said he was stepping out for cigarettes and was never heard from again. Ruth took over raising the family with help from relatives. They traveled throughout many states over several years, finally moving back to Durham, Maine, in 1958.\\n\\nStephen began his actual writing career in January of 1959, when David and Stephen decided to publish their own local newspaper named \\\"Dave's Rag\\\". David bought a mimeograph machine, and they put together a paper they sold for five cents an issue. Stephen attended Lisbon High School, in Lisbon, in 1962. Collaborating with his best friend Chris Chesley in 1963, they published a collection of 18 short stories called \\\"People, Places, and Things--Volume I\\\". King's stories included \\\"Hotel at the End of the Road\\\", \\\"I've Got to Get Away!\\\", \\\"The Dimension Warp\\\", \\\"The Thing at the Bottom of the Well\\\", \\\"The Stranger\\\", \\\"I'm Falling\\\", \\\"The Cursed Expedition\\\", and \\\"The Other Side of the Fog.\\\" A year later, King's amateur press, Triad and Gaslight Books, published a two-part book titled \\\"The Star Invaders\\\".\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1524, \"text_tokens\": 375, \"title_tokens\": 9, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.390977680683136}, {\"docid\": \"61397\", \"url\": \"https://www.onthisday.com/birthdays/date/1965/april\", \"title\": \"Famous People Born in April 1965\", \"title_span\": [11, 43], \"document_sha256\": \"edd2482312dcd3a2f9a7009de36d9937dbca62ae5616014ac6b7f14a062ba69a\", \"window_ref\": \"w_ab5e3c174ad832fb78312d56\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Famous People Born in April 1965\\ndate: 2025-01-01\\n---\\n- Apr 1 John \\\"Jumbo\\\" Elliott, American College Football HOF offensive tackle (Uni of Michigan;         "content": "[{\"docid\": \"63702\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_King\", \"title\": \"Larry King - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 33], \"document_sha256\": \"ccd0ea30e36b6c73bce08123095e0d1517691e6f6d2eee9f7c69358696060741\", \"window_ref\": \"w_a1cc8426e9577920fbe632e5\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Larry King - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases\\ndate: 2003-08-22\\n---\\nname: Larry King\\nbirth_name: Lawrence Harvey Zeiger\\nbirth_date: 19 November 1933\\nbirth_place: New York City, U.S.\\ndeath_place: Los Angeles, California, U.S.\\ndeath_date: 23 January 2021\\noccupation: Radio host, TV host, author, spokesman\\nyears_active: 1957–2021\\nparty: Democratic\\nresting_place: Hillside Memorial Park Cemetery, Culver City, California, U.S.\\nspouse: * * * * * * *\\nchildren: 5\\n\\nLarry King (born Lawrence Harvey Zeiger; November 19, 1933 – January 23, 2021) was an American TV and radio host presenter, author, and former spokesman. He was a WMBM radio interviewer in the Miami area in the 1950s and 1960s and beginning in 1978, gained national prominence as host of The Larry King Show, an all-night nationwide call-in radio program heard over the Mutual Broadcasting System. From 1985 to 2010, he hosted the nightly interview television program Larry King Live on CNN. King hosted Larry King Now from 2012 to 2020, which aired on Hulu, Ora TV, and RT America. He hosted Politicking with Larry King, a weekly political talk show, on the same three channels from 2013 to 2020. King conducted over 50,000 interviews on radio and television.\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1243, \"text_tokens\": 366, \"title_tokens\": 4, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.47633177042007446}, {\"docid\": \"40705\", \"url\": \"https://kinginstitute.stanford.edu/king-resources/major-king-events-chronology-1929-1968\", \"title\": \"Major King Events Chronology: 1929-1968\", \"title_span\": [11, 50], \"document_sha256\": \"47dd4e04088003b13df546daaa4df03492051c6739812d568be3f60990182d21\", \"window_ref\": \"w_bbe9001fe810027a545cadb9\", \"text\": \"King is among the first passengers to ride the buses in an integrated fashion. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1957 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n10-11 January |\\n\\nSouthern black ministers meet in Atlanta to share strategies in the fight against segregation. King is named chairman of the Southern Negro Leaders Conference on Transportation and Nonviolent Integration (later known as the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, SCLC). |\\n\\n|\\n\\n18 February |\\n\\nKing appears on the cover of Time magazine. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n6 March |\\n\\nKing attends the independence celebrations of the new nation of Ghana in West Africa and meets with Prime Minister Kwame Nkrumah. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n17 May |\\n\\nAt the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., King delivers his first national address, \\\"Give Us The Ballot,\\\" at the Prayer Pilgrimage for Freedom. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n13 June |\\n\\nKing and Ralph D. He is best known for his roles in the films The Constant Gardener, The Fifth Estate and Sense8.\\n\\nPersonal life\\n\\nNzioki was born on 25 May 1978 in Nairobi, Kenya. His father Michael David Mwania, served in the Kenyan Army and his mother worked at the military hospital. At the age of six, he joined church productions at the Lang'ata Barracks. He completed his education from Lang'ata High School in Nairobi.\\n\\nHe is married to fellow actress Tess King.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nHe made acting debut in 2000 at the Kenya National Theatre for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanuka. In theater, he played 'Iago' in the Phoenix Players production of the Shakespeare tragedy Othello. In 2005, he made his film debut with a minor role in The Constant Gardener directed by Fernando Meirelles. In the same year, he appeared as 'Barman' in the television movie Transit. In 2016, he appeared in the thriller film The CEO where he played the role of 'Jomo'. \", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1299, \"text_tokens\": 366, \"title_tokens\": 6, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.4395018517971039}, {\"docid\": \"7927\", \"url\": \"https://www.imdb.com/list/ls072153898/\", \"title\": \"80's & 90's Authors\", \"title_span\": [11, 30], \"document_sha256\": \"dba8c853fef3fc3a56776bd0ab903ba6f15ed7e49f1fd2e936fb3d11506cc4e7\", \"window_ref\": \"w_177da5523f166cc0b3a3aa11\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: 80's & 90's Authors\\ndate: 2025-01-01\\n---\\nStephen Edwin King was born on September 21, 1947, at the Maine General Hospital in Portland. His parents were Nellie Ruth (Pillsbury), who worked as a caregiver at a mental institute, and Donald Edwin King, a merchant seaman. His father was born under the surname \\\"Pollock,\\\" but used the last name \\\"King,\\\" under which Stephen was born. He has an older brother, David. The Kings were a typical family until one night, when Donald said he was stepping out for cigarettes and was never heard from again. Ruth took over raising the family with help from relatives. They traveled throughout many states over several years, finally moving back to Durham, Maine, in 1958.\\n\\nStephen began his actual writing career in January of 1959, when David and Stephen decided to publish their own local newspaper named \\\"Dave's Rag\\\". David bought a mimeograph machine, and they put together a paper they sold for five cents an issue. Stephen attended Lisbon High School, in Lisbon, in 1962. Collaborating with his best friend Chris Chesley in 1963, they published a collection of 18 short stories called \\\"People, Places, and Things--Volume I\\\". King's stories included \\\"Hotel at the End of the Road\\\", \\\"I've Got to Get Away!\\\", \\\"The Dimension Warp\\\", \\\"The Thing at the Bottom of the Well\\\", \\\"The Stranger\\\", \\\"I'm Falling\\\", \\\"The Cursed Expedition\\\", and \\\"The Other Side of the Fog.\\\" A year later, King's amateur press, Triad and Gaslight Books, published a two-part book titled \\\"The Star Invaders\\\".\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1524, \"text_tokens\": 375, \"title_tokens\": 9, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.390977680683136}, {\"docid\": \"61397\", \"url\": \"https://www.onthisday.com/birthdays/date/1965/april\", \"title\": \"Famous People Born in April 1965\", \"title_span\": [11, 43], \"document_sha256\": \"edd2482312dcd3a2f9a7009de36d9937dbca62ae5616014ac6b7f14a062ba69a\", \"window_ref\": \"w_ab5e3c174ad832fb78312d56\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Famous People Born in April 1965\\ndate: 2025-01-01\\n---\\n- Apr 1 John \\\"Jumbo\\\" Elliott, American College Football HOF offensive tackle (Uni of Michigan; He studied history at Victoria University of Wellington, working part-time for the Evening Post, and graduated with a BA in 1967. \", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1476, \"text_tokens\": 384, \"title_tokens\": 8, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.40655717253685}, {\"docid\": \"78689\", \"url\": \"https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/04/04/peter-gatien-the-90s-club-king-wants-his-final-say/\", \"title\": \"Peter Gatien, the '90s 'club king,' wants his final say\", \"title_span\": [11, 66], \"document_sha256\": \"6fc78ef0d0a0fafc1d5177aec08acc4536957b265b0e996efae65ba1f6d6d6bd\", \"window_ref\": \"w_1b0b58e2f036d722b7beff25\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Peter Gatien, the '90s 'club king,' wants his final say\\nauthor: The New York Times\\ndate: 2020-04-04\\n---\\nNEW YORK — \\\"Thoughts flash in your mind of incredible nights here, whether it was Jay-Z, or Junior Vasquez, or the thousands of people inside and outside, waiting in line,\\\" said Peter Gatien, the nightclub impresario who lorded over the 1990s club scene in New York City.\\n\\nIt was a brisk Wednesday in early March, a few days before the city shut down because of the new coronavirus, and Gatien was at La Colombe, a cafe inside the brick warehouse that once housed the Tunnel, the massive nightclub on West 27th Street that is now celebrated as a crucible of hip-hop.\\n\\n\\\"Just the raw energy, the exuberance,\\\" he said, sipping an iced tea. \\\"You don't see it anymore.\\\"\\n\\nTimes change. The Tunnel, a former warehouse where Biggie Smalls and Busta Rhymes once barked out raps to frenzied throngs, is converting to offices and luxury retail, blending seamlessly with the gleaming Hudson Yards to the north.\\n\\nAnd Gatien, with his icy demeanor and swashbuckler eye patch, is no longer the \\\"King of Clubs,\\\" as he was hailed by The New York Post in his '90s heyday. His spectacle megaclubs in the city — Limelight, Palladium, Club USA and the Tunnel — were raking in more than $1 million a week at the time, he said, before a drug trial, which he ultimately won, cost him, well, basically, everything.\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1405, \"text_tokens\": 358, \"title_tokens\": 17, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.3848554491996765}]"

        "content": "[{\"docid\": \"40705\", \"url\": \"https://kinginstitute.stanford.edu/king-resources/major-king-events-chronology-1929-1968\", \"title\": \"Major King Events Chronology: 1929-1968\", \"title_span\": [11, 50], \"document_sha256\": \"47dd4e04088003b13df546daaa4df03492051c6739812d568be3f60990182d21\", \"window_ref\": \"w_6a3928912dba6e520ee73d08\", \"text\": \"|\\n\\n1960 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n1 February |\\n\\nKing moves from Montgomery to Atlanta to devote more time to SCLC and the freedom struggle. He becomes assistant pastor to his father at Ebenezer Baptist Church. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n25-28 May |\\n\\nKing is found not guilty of tax fraud by a white jury in Montgomery. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n23 June |\\n\\nKing meets privately in New York with Democratic presidential candidate John F. Kennedy. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n19 October |\\n\\nKing is arrested during a sit-in demonstration at Rich's department store in Atlanta. He is sentenced to four months of hard labor for violating probation conditions he had received earlier that year for driving with an out-of-state driver's license. He is released on $2000 bond on 27 October. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1961 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n31 January |\\n\\nDexter Scott, King's third child, is born. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n21 May |\\n\\nAfter the initial group of Freedom Riders seeking to integrate bus terminals is assaulted in Alabama, King addresses a mass rally at a mob-besieged Montgomery church. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n16 October |\\n\\nKing meets with President John F. Kennedy and urges him to issue a second Emancipation Proclamation to eliminate racial segregation. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n16 December |\\n\\nKing, Ralph Abernathy, Albany Movement president William G. King) — moves from 501 Auburn Avenue to 193 Boulevard in Atlanta. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1944 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n20 September |\\n\\nKing begins his freshman year at Morehouse College in Atlanta. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1946 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n6 August |\\n\\nThe Atlanta Constitution publishes King's letter to the editor stating that black people \\\"are entitled to the basic rights and opportunities of American citizens.\\\" |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1948 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n25 February |\\n\\nKing is ordained and appointed assistant pastor at Ebenezer Baptist Church in Atlanta. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n8 June |\\n\\nKing receives his bachelor of arts degree in sociology from Morehouse College. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n14 September |\\n\\nKing begins his studies at Crozer Theological Seminary in Chester, Pennsylvania. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1951 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n6-8 May |\\n\\nKing graduates from Crozer with a bachelor of divinity degree, delivering the valedictory address at commencement. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n13 September |\\n\\nKing begins his graduate studies in systematic theology at Boston University. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1953 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n18 June |\\n\\nKing and Coretta Scott are married at the Scott home near Marion, Alabama. |\\n\\n|\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1472, \"text_tokens\": 382, \"title_tokens\": 16, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.4553649127483368}, {\"docid\": \"87268\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_King_%28historian%29\", \"title\": \"Michael King (historian) - His Glasgow-born father was an advertising executive who had left New Zealand to serve as a naval officer in World War II and had risen to the rank of lieutenant-commander. King's family moved to Auckland for a while, where he attended Sacred Heart College, then returned to Wellington, where he attended St Patrick's College, Silverstream in Upper Hutt.         "content": "[{\"docid\": \"63702\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_King\", \"title\": \"Larry King - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 33], \"document_sha256\": \"ccd0ea30e36b6c73bce08123095e0d1517691e6f6d2eee9f7c69358696060741\", \"window_ref\": \"w_a1cc8426e9577920fbe632e5\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Larry King - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases\\ndate: 2003-08-22\\n---\\nname: Larry King\\nbirth_name: Lawrence Harvey Zeiger\\nbirth_date: 19 November 1933\\nbirth_place: New York City, U.S.\\ndeath_place: Los Angeles, California, U.S.\\ndeath_date: 23 January 2021\\noccupation: Radio host, TV host, author, spokesman\\nyears_active: 1957–2021\\nparty: Democratic\\nresting_place: Hillside Memorial Park Cemetery, Culver City, California, U.S.\\nspouse: * * * * * * *\\nchildren: 5\\n\\nLarry King (born Lawrence Harvey Zeiger; November 19, 1933 – January 23, 2021) was an American TV and radio host presenter, author, and former spokesman. He was a WMBM radio interviewer in the Miami area in the 1950s and 1960s and beginning in 1978, gained national prominence as host of The Larry King Show, an all-night nationwide call-in radio program heard over the Mutual Broadcasting System. From 1985 to 2010, he hosted the nightly interview television program Larry King Live on CNN. King hosted Larry King Now from 2012 to 2020, which aired on Hulu, Ora TV, and RT America. He hosted Politicking with Larry King, a weekly political talk show, on the same three channels from 2013 to 2020. King conducted over 50,000 interviews on radio and television.\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1243, \"text_tokens\": 366, \"title_tokens\": 4, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.47633177042007446}, {\"docid\": \"40705\", \"url\": \"https://kinginstitute.stanford.edu/king-resources/major-king-events-chronology-1929-1968\", \"title\": \"Major King Events Chronology: 1929-1968\", \"title_span\": [11, 50], \"document_sha256\": \"47dd4e04088003b13df546daaa4df03492051c6739812d568be3f60990182d21\", \"window_ref\": \"w_bbe9001fe810027a545cadb9\", \"text\": \"King is among the first passengers to ride the buses in an integrated fashion. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1957 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n10-11 January |\\n\\nSouthern black ministers meet in Atlanta to share strategies in the fight against segregation. King is named chairman of the Southern Negro Leaders Conference on Transportation and Nonviolent Integration (later known as the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, SCLC). |\\n\\n|\\n\\n18 February |\\n\\nKing appears on the cover of Time magazine. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n6 March |\\n\\nKing attends the independence celebrations of the new nation of Ghana in West Africa and meets with Prime Minister Kwame Nkrumah. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n17 May |\\n\\nAt the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., King delivers his first national address, \\\"Give Us The Ballot,\\\" at the Prayer Pilgrimage for Freedom. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n13 June |\\n\\nKing and Ralph D. Abernathy meet with Vice President Richard M. He is rushed to Harlem Hospital, where a team of doctors successfully remove a seven-inch letter opener from his chest. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1959 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n3 February |\\n\\nKing embarks on a month-long visit to India, where he meets with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and many of Gandhi's followers. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1960 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n1 February |\\n\", \"offset\": 2966, \"end_char\": 4603, \"text_tokens\": 374, \"title_tokens\": 16, \"has_more_before\": true, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.44736021757125854}, {\"docid\": \"67431\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki\", \"title\": \"Peter Nzioki - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 35], \"document_sha256\": \"df105e9610723015216b9cc93b7e7d9b84055f287422d1f577946fdb0b99d860\", \"window_ref\": \"w_847088d110a745604b5159e5\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Peter Nzioki - Wikipedia\\ndate: 2020-11-06\\n---\\nname: Peter King Nzioki Mwania\\nbirth_date: 25 May 1978\\nbirth_name: Peter King Nzioki Mwania\\nbirth_place: Kenya\\nnationality: Kenyan\\nheight: 1.8 m\\nyears_active: 2000–present\\nspouse: Tess King\\noccupation: Actor\\n\\nPeter King Nzioki Mwania (born 25 May 1978), popularly known as Peter King, is a Kenyan actor. He is best known for his roles in the films The Constant Gardener, The Fifth Estate and Sense8.\\n\\nPersonal life\\n\\nNzioki was born on 25 May 1978 in Nairobi, Kenya. His father Michael David Mwania, served in the Kenyan Army and his mother worked at the military hospital. At the age of six, he joined church productions at the Lang'ata Barracks. He completed his education from Lang'ata High School in Nairobi.\\n\\nHe is married to fellow actress Tess King.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nHe made acting debut in 2000 at the Kenya National Theatre for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanuka. In theater, he played 'Iago' in the Phoenix Players production of the Shakespeare tragedy Othello. In 2005, he made his film debut with a minor role in The Constant Gardener directed by Fernando Meirelles. In the same year, he appeared as 'Barman' in the television movie Transit. In 2016, he appeared in the thriller film The CEO where he played the role of 'Jomo'. \", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1299, \"text_tokens\": 366, \"title_tokens\": 6, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.4395018517971039}, {\"docid\": \"7927\", \"url\": \"https://www.imdb.com/list/ls072153898/\", \"title\": \"80's & 90's Authors\", \"title_span\": [11, 30], \"document_sha256\": \"dba8c853fef3fc3a56776bd0ab903ba6f15ed7e49f1fd2e936fb3d11506cc4e7\", \"window_ref\": \"w_177da5523f166cc0b3a3aa11\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: 80's & 90's Authors\\ndate: 2025-01-01\\n---\\nStephen Edwin King was born on September 21, 1947, at the Maine General Hospital in Portland. His parents were Nellie Ruth (Pillsbury), who worked as a caregiver at a mental institute, and Donald Edwin King, a merchant seaman. His father was born under the surname \\\"Pollock,\\\" but used the last name \\\"King,\\\" under which Stephen was born. He has an older brother, David. The Kings were a typical family until one night, when Donald said he was stepping out for cigarettes and was never heard from again. Ruth took over raising the family with help from relatives. They traveled throughout many states over several years, finally moving back to Durham, Maine, in 1958.\\n\\nStephen began his actual writing career in January of 1959, when David and Stephen decided to publish their own local newspaper named \\\"Dave's Rag\\\". David bought a mimeograph machine, and they put together a paper they sold for five cents an issue. Stephen attended Lisbon High School, in Lisbon, in 1962. Collaborating with his best friend Chris Chesley in 1963, they published a collection of 18 short stories called \\\"People, Places, and Things--Volume I\\\". King's stories included \\\"Hotel at the End of the Road\\\", \\\"I've Got to Get Away!\\\", \\\"The Dimension Warp\\\", \\\"The Thing at the Bottom of the Well\\\", \\\"The Stranger\\\", \\\"I'm Falling\\\", \\\"The Cursed Expedition\\\", and \\\"The Other Side of the Fog.\\\" A year later, King's amateur press, Triad and Gaslight Books, published a two-part book titled \\\"The Star Invaders\\\".\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1524, \"text_tokens\": 375, \"title_tokens\": 9, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.390977680683136}, {\"docid\": \"61397\", \"url\": \"https://www.onthisday.com/birthdays/date/1965/april\", \"title\": \"Famous People Born in April 1965\", \"title_span\": [11, 43], \"document_sha256\": \"edd2482312dcd3a2f9a7009de36d9937dbca62ae5616014ac6b7f14a062ba69a\", \"window_ref\": \"w_ab5e3c174ad832fb78312d56\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Famous People Born in April 1965\\ndate: 2025-01-01\\n---\\n- Apr 1 John \\\"Jumbo\\\" Elliott, American College Football HOF offensive tackle (Uni of Michigan; The Tunnel, a former warehouse where Biggie Smalls and Busta Rhymes once barked out raps to frenzied throngs, is converting to offices and luxury retail, blending seamlessly with the gleaming Hudson Yards to the north.\\n\\nAnd Gatien, with his icy demeanor and swashbuckler eye patch, is no longer the \\\"King of Clubs,\\\" as he was hailed by The New York Post in his '90s heyday. King occasionally entertained the audience by telling amusing stories from his youth or early broadcasting career.\\n\\nWishing to reduce his workload, King began hosting a shorter, daytime version of the show in 1993. Jim Bohannon, King's primary fill-in host, took over the late night time slot. After 16 years on Mutual, King decided to retire from the program. The final broadcast of The Larry King Show was heard on May 27, 1994; Mutual gave King's afternoon slot to David Brenner and Mutual's affiliates were given the option of carrying the audio of King's new CNN evening television program. The fight between Ali and Foreman was a much-anticipated event. His parents were Nellie Ruth (Pillsbury), who worked as a caregiver at a mental institute, and Donald Edwin King, a merchant seaman. His father was born under the surname \\\"Pollock,\\\" but used the last name \\\"King,\\\" under which Stephen was born. He has an older brother, David. The Kings were a typical family until one night, when Donald said he was stepping out for cigarettes and was never heard from again. Ruth took over raising the family with help from relatives. They traveled throughout many states over several years, finally moving back to Durham, Maine, in 1958.\\n\\nStephen began his actual writing career in January of 1959, when David and Stephen decided to publish their own local newspaper named \\\"Dave's Rag\\\". David bought a mimeograph machine, and they put together a paper they sold for five cents an issue. Stephen attended Lisbon High School, in Lisbon, in 1962. Collaborating with his best friend Chris Chesley in 1963, they published a collection of 18 short stories called \\\"People, Places, and Things--Volume I\\\". From 1985 to 2010, he hosted the nightly interview television program Larry King Live on CNN. King hosted Larry King Now from 2012 to 2020, which aired on Hulu, Ora TV, and RT America. He hosted Politicking with Larry King, a weekly political talk show, on the same three channels from 2013 to 2020. King is named chairman of the Southern Negro Leaders Conference on Transportation and Nonviolent Integration (later known as the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, SCLC). |\\n\\n|\\n\\n18 February |\\n\\nKing appears on the cover of Time magazine. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n6 March |\\n\\nKing attends the independence celebrations of the new nation of Ghana in West Africa and meets with Prime Minister Kwame Nkrumah. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n17 May |\\n\\nAt the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., King delivers his first national address, \\\"Give Us The Ballot,\\\" at the Prayer Pilgrimage for Freedom. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n13 June |\\n\\nKing and Ralph D. He studied history at Victoria University of Wellington, working part-time for the Evening Post, and graduated with a BA in 1967. \", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1476, \"text_tokens\": 384, \"title_tokens\": 8, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.40655717253685}, {\"docid\": \"78689\", \"url\": \"https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/04/04/peter-gatien-the-90s-club-king-wants-his-final-say/\", \"title\": \"Peter Gatien, the '90s 'club king,' wants his final say\", \"title_span\": [11, 66], \"document_sha256\": \"6fc78ef0d0a0fafc1d5177aec08acc4536957b265b0e996efae65ba1f6d6d6bd\", \"window_ref\": \"w_1b0b58e2f036d722b7beff25\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Peter Gatien, the '90s 'club king,' wants his final say\\nauthor: The New York Times\\ndate: 2020-04-04\\n---\\nNEW YORK — \\\"Thoughts flash in your mind of incredible nights here, whether it was Jay-Z, or Junior Vasquez, or the thousands of people inside and outside, waiting in line,\\\" said Peter Gatien, the nightclub impresario who lorded over the 1990s club scene in New York City.\\n\\nIt was a brisk Wednesday in early March, a few days before the city shut down because of the new coronavirus, and Gatien was at La Colombe, a cafe inside the brick warehouse that once housed the Tunnel, the massive nightclub on West 27th Street that is now celebrated as a crucible of hip-hop.\\n\\n\\\"Just the raw energy, the exuberance,\\\" he said, sipping an iced tea. \\\"You don't see it anymore.\\\"\\n\\nTimes change. The Tunnel, a former warehouse where Biggie Smalls and Busta Rhymes once barked out raps to frenzied throngs, is converting to offices and luxury retail, blending seamlessly with the gleaming Hudson Yards to the north.\\n\\nAnd Gatien, with his icy demeanor and swashbuckler eye patch, is no longer the \\\"King of Clubs,\\\" as he was hailed by The New York Post in his '90s heyday. His spectacle megaclubs in the city — Limelight, Palladium, Club USA and the Tunnel — were raking in more than $1 million a week at the time, he said, before a drug trial, which he ultimately won, cost him, well, basically, everything.\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1405, \"text_tokens\": 358, \"title_tokens\": 17, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.3848554491996765}]"

        "content": "[{\"docid\": \"40705\", \"url\": \"https://kinginstitute.stanford.edu/king-resources/major-king-events-chronology-1929-1968\", \"title\": \"Major King Events Chronology: 1929-1968\", \"title_span\": [11, 50], \"document_sha256\": \"47dd4e04088003b13df546daaa4df03492051c6739812d568be3f60990182d21\", \"window_ref\": \"w_6a3928912dba6e520ee73d08\", \"text\": \"|\\n\\n1960 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n1 February |\\n\\nKing moves from Montgomery to Atlanta to devote more time to SCLC and the freedom struggle. He becomes assistant pastor to his father at Ebenezer Baptist Church. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n25-28 May |\\n\\nKing is found not guilty of tax fraud by a white jury in Montgomery. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n23 June |\\n\\nKing meets privately in New York with Democratic presidential candidate John F. Kennedy. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n19 October |\\n\\nKing is arrested during a sit-in demonstration at Rich's department store in Atlanta. He is sentenced to four months of hard labor for violating probation conditions he had received earlier that year for driving with an out-of-state driver's license. He is released on $2000 bond on 27 October. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1961 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n31 January |\\n\\nDexter Scott, King's third child, is born. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n21 May |\\n\\nAfter the initial group of Freedom Riders seeking to integrate bus terminals is assaulted in Alabama, King addresses a mass rally at a mob-besieged Montgomery church. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n16 October |\\n\\nKing meets with President John F. Kennedy and urges him to issue a second Emancipation Proclamation to eliminate racial segregation. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n16 December |\\n\\nKing, Ralph Abernathy, Albany Movement president William G. Anderson, and other protesters are arrested by Laurie Pritchett during a campaign in Albany, Georgia. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1962 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n27 July-10 August |\\n\\nKing is arrested at an Albany, Georgia prayer vigil and jailed. After spending two weeks in jail, King is released. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n28 September |\\n\\nDuring the closing session of the SCLC conference in Birmingham, Alabama, a member of the American Nazi Party assaults King, striking him twice in the face. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1963 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n28 March |\\n\", \"offset\": 4575, \"end_char\": 6232, \"text_tokens\": 382, \"title_tokens\": 16, \"has_more_before\": true, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.5530825853347778}, {\"docid\": \"63702\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_King\", \"title\": \"Larry King - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 33], \"document_sha256\": \"ccd0ea30e36b6c73bce08123095e0d1517691e6f6d2eee9f7c69358696060741\", \"window_ref\": \"w_c245563b7cf525db4038a447\", \"text\": \"At the beginning, the show had 28 affiliates, but eventually rose to over 500. King occasionally entertained the audience by telling amusing stories from his youth or early broadcasting career.\\n\\nWishing to reduce his workload, King began hosting a shorter, daytime version of the show in 1993. Jim Bohannon, King's primary fill-in host, took over the late night time slot. After 16 years on Mutual, King decided to retire from the program. The final broadcast of The Larry King Show was heard on May 27, 1994; Mutual gave King's afternoon slot to David Brenner and Mutual's affiliates were given the option of carrying the audio of King's new CNN evening television program. After Westwood One dissolved Mutual in 1999, the radio simulcast of the CNN show continued until December 31, 2009.\\n\\nLarry King Live\\n\\nLarry King Live began on CNN in June 1985. King hosted a broad range of guests, from figures such as UFO conspiracy theorists and alleged psychics,One notable guest was Sylvia Browne, who in 2005 told the Newsweek magazine that King, a believer in the paranormal, asks her to do private psychic readings. to prominent politicians and entertainment industry figures, often giving their first or only interview on breaking news stories on his show. After broadcasting his CNN show from 9 to 10 p.m., King then traveled to the studios of the Mutual Broadcasting System to do his radio show, when both shows still aired.\\n\\nTwo of his best-remembered interviews involved political figures. In 1992, billionaire Ross Perot announced his presidential bid on the show. In 1993, a debate between Al Gore and Perot became CNN's most-watched segment until 2015.\\n\", \"offset\": 7214, \"end_char\": 8873, \"text_tokens\": 382, \"title_tokens\": 4, \"has_more_before\": true, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.5369002819061279}, {\"docid\": \"14697\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_King\", \"title\": \"Don King - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 31], \"document_sha256\": \"6e2927cac17bea0769ee88262b0e5dfb92cd37b0452208be9640e63b01499193\", \"window_ref\": \"w_0f5d612fea2aacaac49be82e\", \"text\": \"That gave me an Enlightenment on life that don't get mad, get smart. That's why I want other kids to educate themselves, put it in their brain, they can't take that away.\\\"\\nI learned this here, in the ... penitentiary, in reading everything that I can find my hands on, and didn't living the life that I live before I got to the penitentiary. That gave me an enlightenment on life that \\\"don't get mad, get smart.\\\" That's why I want other kids to educate themselves, put it in their brain, they can't take that away.\\n\\nIn 1972 after serving three years and eleven months, King was released when his attorney got the conviction reduced to manslaughter. King was pardoned in 1983 by Ohio Governor Jim Rhodes, with letters from Jesse Jackson, Coretta Scott King, George Voinovich, Art Modell, and Gabe Paul, among others, being written in support of King.\\\"SPORTS PEOPLE; Don King Pardoned\\\", The New York Times, January 5, 1983. Accessed May 29, 2011.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nKing entered the boxing world after convincing Muhammad Ali to box in a charity exhibition for a local hospital in Cleveland with the help of singer Lloyd Price. Early on, he formed a partnership with a local promoter named Don Elbaum, who already had a stable of fighters in Cleveland and years of experience in boxing. In 1974, King negotiated to promote a heavyweight championship fight between Muhammad Ali and George Foreman in Zaire, popularly known as \\\"The Rumble in the Jungle\\\". The fight between Ali and Foreman was a much-anticipated event. King's rivals all sought to promote the bout, but King was able to secure the then-record $10 million purse through an arrangement with the government of Zaire.\\n\", \"offset\": 4481, \"end_char\": 6147, \"text_tokens\": 389, \"title_tokens\": 4, \"has_more_before\": true, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.4662218689918518}, {\"docid\": \"87268\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_King_%28historian%29\", \"title\": \"Michael King (historian) - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 47], \"document_sha256\": \"5a814e7837d2ed3ff096c36e81d23c1a56819b5c834bca204cc21ea5cd1645e4\", \"window_ref\": \"w_1a9e7ac7fa5db85d1f774266\", \"text\": \"author: Authority control databases\\ndate: 2004-03-30\\n---\\nname: Michael King\\nhonorific_suffix: NZL OBE 100%\\nbirth_date: 15 December 1945\\nbirth_place: Wellington, New Zealand\\ndeath_date: 30 03 2004\\ndeath_place: near Maramarua, Waikato, New Zealand\\noccupation: Historian, biographer\\nalma_mater: Victoria University of Wellington, University of Waikato\\nnotableworks: The Penguin History of New Zealand\\nrelatives: Jonathan King (son)Rachael King (daughter)\\nawards: Officer of the Order of the British Empire (1988)Prime Minister's Award for Literary Achievement (2003)\\n\\nMichael King (15 December 1945 – 30 March 2004) was a New Zealand historian, author, and biographer. He wrote or edited over 30 books on New Zealand topics, including the best-selling Penguin History of New Zealand, which was the most popular New Zealand book of 2004.\\n\\nLife\\n\\nKing was born in Wellington, one of four children to Eleanor and Lewis King, and grew up at Paremata. His Glasgow-born father was an advertising executive who had left New Zealand to serve as a naval officer in World War II and had risen to the rank of lieutenant-commander. His parents were Nellie Ruth (Pillsbury), who worked as a caregiver at a mental institute, and Donald Edwin King, a merchant seaman. His father was born under the surname \\\"Pollock,\\\" but used the last name \\\"King,\\\" under which Stephen was born. He has an older brother, David. The Kings were a typical family until one night, when Donald said he was stepping out for cigarettes and was never heard from again. Ruth took over raising the family with help from relatives. They traveled throughout many states over several years, finally moving back to Durham, Maine, in 1958.\\n\\nStephen began his actual writing career in January of 1959, when David and Stephen decided to publish their own local newspaper named \\\"Dave's Rag\\\". David bought a mimeograph machine, and they put together a paper they sold for five cents an issue. Stephen attended Lisbon High School, in Lisbon, in 1962. Collaborating with his best friend Chris Chesley in 1963, they published a collection of 18 short stories called \\\"People, Places, and Things--Volume I\\\". King's stories included \\\"Hotel at the End of the Road\\\", \\\"I've Got to Get Away!\\\", \\\"The Dimension Warp\\\", \\\"The Thing at the Bottom of the Well\\\", \\\"The Stranger\\\", \\\"I'm Falling\\\", \\\"The Cursed Expedition\\\", and \\\"The Other Side of the Fog.\\\" A year later, King's amateur press, Triad and Gaslight Books, published a two-part book titled \\\"The Star Invaders\\\".\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1524, \"text_tokens\": 375, \"title_tokens\": 9, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.390977680683136}, {\"docid\": \"61397\", \"url\": \"https://www.onthisday.com/birthdays/date/1965/april\", \"title\": \"Famous People Born in April 1965\", \"title_span\": [11, 43], \"document_sha256\": \"edd2482312dcd3a2f9a7009de36d9937dbca62ae5616014ac6b7f14a062ba69a\", \"window_ref\": \"w_ab5e3c174ad832fb78312d56\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Famous People Born in April 1965\\ndate: 2025-01-01\\n---\\n- Apr 1 John \\\"Jumbo\\\" Elliott, American College Football HOF offensive tackle (Uni of Michigan;         "content": "[{\"docid\": \"63702\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_King\", \"title\": \"Larry King - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 33], \"document_sha256\": \"ccd0ea30e36b6c73bce08123095e0d1517691e6f6d2eee9f7c69358696060741\", \"window_ref\": \"w_a1cc8426e9577920fbe632e5\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Larry King - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases\\ndate: 2003-08-22\\n---\\nname: Larry King\\nbirth_name: Lawrence Harvey Zeiger\\nbirth_date: 19 November 1933\\nbirth_place: New York City, U.S.\\ndeath_place: Los Angeles, California, U.S.\\ndeath_date: 23 January 2021\\noccupation: Radio host, TV host, author, spokesman\\nyears_active: 1957–2021\\nparty: Democratic\\nresting_place: Hillside Memorial Park Cemetery, Culver City, California, U.S.\\nspouse: * * * * * * *\\nchildren: 5\\n\\nLarry King (born Lawrence Harvey Zeiger; November 19, 1933 – January 23, 2021) was an American TV and radio host presenter, author, and former spokesman. He was a WMBM radio interviewer in the Miami area in the 1950s and 1960s and beginning in 1978, gained national prominence as host of The Larry King Show, an all-night nationwide call-in radio program heard over the Mutual Broadcasting System. From 1985 to 2010, he hosted the nightly interview television program Larry King Live on CNN. King hosted Larry King Now from 2012 to 2020, which aired on Hulu, Ora TV, and RT America. He hosted Politicking with Larry King, a weekly political talk show, on the same three channels from 2013 to 2020. King conducted over 50,000 interviews on radio and television.\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1243, \"text_tokens\": 366, \"title_tokens\": 4, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.4929233193397522}, {\"docid\": \"67431\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki\", \"title\": \"Peter Nzioki - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 35], \"document_sha256\": \"df105e9610723015216b9cc93b7e7d9b84055f287422d1f577946fdb0b99d860\", \"window_ref\": \"w_847088d110a745604b5159e5\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Peter Nzioki - Wikipedia\\ndate: 2020-11-06\\n---\\nname: Peter King Nzioki Mwania\\nbirth_date: 25 May 1978\\nbirth_name: Peter King Nzioki Mwania\\nbirth_place: Kenya\\nnationality: Kenyan\\nheight: 1.8 m\\nyears_active: 2000–present\\nspouse: Tess King\\noccupation: Actor\\n\\nPeter King Nzioki Mwania (born 25 May 1978), popularly known as Peter King, is a Kenyan actor. King is named chairman of the Southern Negro Leaders Conference on Transportation and Nonviolent Integration (later known as the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, SCLC). |\\n\\n|\\n\\n18 February |\\n\\nKing appears on the cover of Time magazine. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n6 March |\\n\\nKing attends the independence celebrations of the new nation of Ghana in West Africa and meets with Prime Minister Kwame Nkrumah. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n17 May |\\n\\nAt the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., King delivers his first national address, \\\"Give Us The Ballot,\\\" at the Prayer Pilgrimage for Freedom. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n13 June |\\n\\nKing and Ralph D. He is rushed to Harlem Hospital, where a team of doctors successfully remove a seven-inch letter opener from his chest. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1959 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n3 February |\\n\\nKing embarks on a month-long visit to India, where he meets with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and many of Gandhi's followers. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1960 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n1 February |\\n\", \"offset\": 2966, \"end_char\": 4603, \"text_tokens\": 374, \"title_tokens\": 16, \"has_more_before\": true, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.4530163109302521}, {\"docid\": \"87268\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_King_%28historian%29\", \"title\": \"Michael King (historian) - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 47], \"document_sha256\": \"5a814e7837d2ed3ff096c36e81d23c1a56819b5c834bca204cc21ea5cd1645e4\", \"window_ref\": \"w_bab6b20e04a9905f53333c2b\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Michael King (historian) - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases\\ndate: 2004-03-30\\n---\\nname: Michael King\\nhonorific_suffix: NZL OBE 100%\\nbirth_date: 15 December 1945\\nbirth_place: Wellington, New Zealand\\ndeath_date: 30 03 2004\\ndeath_place: near Maramarua, Waikato, New Zealand\\noccupation: Historian, biographer\\nalma_mater: Victoria University of Wellington, University of Waikato\\nnotableworks: The Penguin History of New Zealand\\nrelatives: Jonathan King (son)Rachael King (daughter)\\nawards: Officer of the Order of the British Empire (1988)Prime Minister's Award for Literary Achievement (2003)\\n\\nMichael King (15 December 1945 – 30 March 2004) was a New Zealand historian, author, and biographer. King's family moved to Auckland for a while, where he attended Sacred Heart College, then returned to Wellington, where he attended St Patrick's College, Silverstream in Upper Hutt. He studied history at Victoria University of Wellington, working part-time for the Evening Post, and graduated with a BA in 1967. \", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1476, \"text_tokens\": 384, \"title_tokens\": 8, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.40655717253685}, {\"docid\": \"78689\", \"url\": \"https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/04/04/peter-gatien-the-90s-club-king-wants-his-final-say/\", \"title\": \"Peter Gatien, the '90s 'club king,' wants his final say\", \"title_span\": [11, 66], \"document_sha256\": \"6fc78ef0d0a0fafc1d5177aec08acc4536957b265b0e996efae65ba1f6d6d6bd\", \"window_ref\": \"w_1b0b58e2f036d722b7beff25\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Peter Gatien, the '90s 'club king,' wants his final say\\nauthor: The New York Times\\ndate: 2020-04-04\\n---\\nNEW YORK — \\\"Thoughts flash in your mind of incredible nights here, whether it was Jay-Z, or Junior Vasquez, or the thousands of people inside and outside, waiting in line,\\\" said Peter Gatien, the nightclub impresario who lorded over the 1990s club scene in New York City.\\n\\nIt was a brisk Wednesday in early March, a few days before the city shut down because of the new coronavirus, and Gatien was at La Colombe, a cafe inside the brick warehouse that once housed the Tunnel, the massive nightclub on West 27th Street that is now celebrated as a crucible of hip-hop.\\n\\n\\\"Just the raw energy, the exuberance,\\\" he said, sipping an iced tea. \\\"You don't see it anymore.\\\"\\n\\nTimes change. The Tunnel, a former warehouse where Biggie Smalls and Busta Rhymes once barked out raps to frenzied throngs, is converting to offices and luxury retail, blending seamlessly with the gleaming Hudson Yards to the north.\\n\\nAnd Gatien, with his icy demeanor and swashbuckler eye patch, is no longer the \\\"King of Clubs,\\\" as he was hailed by The New York Post in his '90s heyday. His spectacle megaclubs in the city — Limelight, Palladium, Club USA and the Tunnel — were raking in more than $1 million a week at the time, he said, before a drug trial, which he ultimately won, cost him, well, basically, everything.\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1405, \"text_tokens\": 358, \"title_tokens\": 17, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.3848554491996765}]"

After spending two weeks in jail, King is released. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n28 September |\\n\\nDuring the closing session of the SCLC conference in Birmingham, Alabama, a member of the American Nazi Party assaults King, striking him twice in the face. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1963 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n28 March |\\n\", \"offset\": 4575, \"end_char\": 6232, \"text_tokens\": 382, \"title_tokens\": 16, \"has_more_before\": true, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.5530825853347778}, {\"docid\": \"63702\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_King\", \"title\": \"Larry King - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 33], \"document_sha256\": \"ccd0ea30e36b6c73bce08123095e0d1517691e6f6d2eee9f7c69358696060741\", \"window_ref\": \"w_c245563b7cf525db4038a447\", \"text\": \"At the beginning, the show had 28 affiliates, but eventually rose to over 500. King occasionally entertained the audience by telling amusing stories from his youth or early broadcasting career.\\n\\nWishing to reduce his workload, King began hosting a shorter, daytime version of the show in 1993. Jim Bohannon, King's primary fill-in host, took over the late night time slot. After 16 years on Mutual, King decided to retire from the program. The final broadcast of The Larry King Show was heard on May 27, 1994; Mutual gave King's afternoon slot to David Brenner and Mutual's affiliates were given the option of carrying the audio of King's new CNN evening television program. After Westwood One dissolved Mutual in 1999, the radio simulcast of the CNN show continued until December 31, 2009.\\n\\nLarry King Live\\n\\nLarry King Live began on CNN in June 1985. King hosted a broad range of guests, from figures such as UFO conspiracy theorists and alleged psychics,One notable guest was Sylvia Browne, who in 2005 told the Newsweek magazine that King, a believer in the paranormal, asks her to do private psychic readings. to prominent politicians and entertainment industry figures, often giving their first or only interview on breaking news stories on his show. After broadcasting his CNN show from 9 to 10 p.m., King then traveled to the studios of the Mutual Broadcasting System to do his radio show, when both shows still aired.\\n\\nTwo of his best-remembered interviews involved political figures. In 1992, billionaire Ross Perot announced his presidential bid on the show. In 1993, a debate between Al Gore and Perot became CNN's most-watched segment until 2015.\\n\", \"offset\": 7214, \"end_char\": 8873, \"text_tokens\": 382, \"title_tokens\": 4, \"has_more_before\": true, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.5369002819061279}, {\"docid\": \"14697\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_King\", \"title\": \"Don King - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 31], \"document_sha256\": \"6e2927cac17bea0769ee88262b0e5dfb92cd37b0452208be9640e63b01499193\", \"window_ref\": \"w_0f5d612fea2aacaac49be82e\", \"text\": \"That gave me an Enlightenment on life that don't get mad, get smart. That's why I want other kids to educate themselves, put it in their brain, they can't take that away.\\\"\\nI learned this here, in the ... penitentiary, in reading everything that I can find my hands on, and didn't living the life that I live before I got to the penitentiary. That gave me an enlightenment on life that \\\"don't get mad, get smart.\\\" That's why I want other kids to educate themselves, put it in their brain, they can't take that away.\\n\\nIn 1972 after serving three years and eleven months, King was released when his attorney got the conviction reduced to manslaughter. King was pardoned in 1983 by Ohio Governor Jim Rhodes, with letters from Jesse Jackson, Coretta Scott King, George Voinovich, Art Modell, and Gabe Paul, among others, being written in support of King.\\\"SPORTS PEOPLE; Don King Pardoned\\\", The New York Times, January 5, 1983. Accessed May 29, 2011.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nKing entered the boxing world after convincing Muhammad Ali to box in a charity exhibition for a local hospital in Cleveland with the help of singer Lloyd Price. He was a WMBM radio interviewer in the Miami area in the 1950s and 1960s and beginning in 1978, gained national prominence as host of The Larry King Show, an all-night nationwide call-in radio program heard over the Mutual Broadcasting System. From 1985 to 2010, he hosted the nightly interview television program Larry King Live on CNN. King hosted Larry King Now from 2012 to 2020, which aired on Hulu, Ora TV, and RT America. He hosted Politicking with Larry King, a weekly political talk show, on the same three channels from 2013 to 2020.         "content": "[{\"docid\": \"63702\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_King\", \"title\": \"Larry King - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 33], \"document_sha256\": \"ccd0ea30e36b6c73bce08123095e0d1517691e6f6d2eee9f7c69358696060741\", \"window_ref\": \"w_a1cc8426e9577920fbe632e5\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Larry King - Wikipedia\\nauthor: Authority control databases\\ndate: 2003-08-22\\n---\\nname: Larry King\\nbirth_name: Lawrence Harvey Zeiger\\nbirth_date: 19 November 1933\\nbirth_place: New York City, U.S.\\ndeath_place: Los Angeles, California, U.S.\\ndeath_date: 23 January 2021\\noccupation: Radio host, TV host, author, spokesman\\nyears_active: 1957–2021\\nparty: Democratic\\nresting_place: Hillside Memorial Park Cemetery, Culver City, California, U.S.\\nspouse: * * * * * * *\\nchildren: 5\\n\\nLarry King (born Lawrence Harvey Zeiger; November 19, 1933 – January 23, 2021) was an American TV and radio host presenter, author, and former spokesman. He was a WMBM radio interviewer in the Miami area in the 1950s and 1960s and beginning in 1978, gained national prominence as host of The Larry King Show, an all-night nationwide call-in radio program heard over the Mutual Broadcasting System. From 1985 to 2010, he hosted the nightly interview television program Larry King Live on CNN. King hosted Larry King Now from 2012 to 2020, which aired on Hulu, Ora TV, and RT America. He hosted Politicking with Larry King, a weekly political talk show, on the same three channels from 2013 to 2020. King conducted over 50,000 interviews on radio and television.\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1243, \"text_tokens\": 366, \"title_tokens\": 4, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.47633177042007446}, {\"docid\": \"40705\", \"url\": \"https://kinginstitute.stanford.edu/king-resources/major-king-events-chronology-1929-1968\", \"title\": \"Major King Events Chronology: 1929-1968\", \"title_span\": [11, 50], \"document_sha256\": \"47dd4e04088003b13df546daaa4df03492051c6739812d568be3f60990182d21\", \"window_ref\": \"w_bbe9001fe810027a545cadb9\", \"text\": \"King is among the first passengers to ride the buses in an integrated fashion. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1957 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n10-11 January |\\n\\nSouthern black ministers meet in Atlanta to share strategies in the fight against segregation. King is named chairman of the Southern Negro Leaders Conference on Transportation and Nonviolent Integration (later known as the Southern Christian Leadership Conference, SCLC). |\\n\\n|\\n\\n18 February |\\n\\nKing appears on the cover of Time magazine. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n6 March |\\n\\nKing attends the independence celebrations of the new nation of Ghana in West Africa and meets with Prime Minister Kwame Nkrumah. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n17 May |\\n\\nAt the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C., King delivers his first national address, \\\"Give Us The Ballot,\\\" at the Prayer Pilgrimage for Freedom. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n13 June |\\n\\nKing and Ralph D. Abernathy meet with Vice President Richard M. He is rushed to Harlem Hospital, where a team of doctors successfully remove a seven-inch letter opener from his chest. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1959 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n3 February |\\n\\nKing embarks on a month-long visit to India, where he meets with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and many of Gandhi's followers. |\\n\\n|\\n\\n1960 |\\n\\n||\\n\\n1 February |\\n\", \"offset\": 2966, \"end_char\": 4603, \"text_tokens\": 374, \"title_tokens\": 16, \"has_more_before\": true, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.44736021757125854}, {\"docid\": \"67431\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki\", \"title\": \"Peter Nzioki - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 35], \"document_sha256\": \"df105e9610723015216b9cc93b7e7d9b84055f287422d1f577946fdb0b99d860\", \"window_ref\": \"w_847088d110a745604b5159e5\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Peter Nzioki - Wikipedia\\ndate: 2020-11-06\\n---\\nname: Peter King Nzioki Mwania\\nbirth_date: 25 May 1978\\nbirth_name: Peter King Nzioki Mwania\\nbirth_place: Kenya\\nnationality: Kenyan\\nheight: 1.8 m\\nyears_active: 2000–present\\nspouse: Tess King\\noccupation: Actor\\n\\nPeter King Nzioki Mwania (born 25 May 1978), popularly known as Peter King, is a Kenyan actor. He is best known for his roles in the films The Constant Gardener, The Fifth Estate and Sense8.\\n\\nPersonal life\\n\\nNzioki was born on 25 May 1978 in Nairobi, Kenya. His father Michael David Mwania, served in the Kenyan Army and his mother worked at the military hospital. At the age of six, he joined church productions at the Lang'ata Barracks. He completed his education from Lang'ata High School in Nairobi.\\n\\nHe is married to fellow actress Tess King.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nHe made acting debut in 2000 at the Kenya National Theatre for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanuka. In theater, he played 'Iago' in the Phoenix Players production of the Shakespeare tragedy Othello. In 2005, he made his film debut with a minor role in The Constant Gardener directed by Fernando Meirelles. In the same year, he appeared as 'Barman' in the television movie Transit. In 2016, he appeared in the thriller film The CEO where he played the role of 'Jomo'. \", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1299, \"text_tokens\": 366, \"title_tokens\": 6, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.4395018517971039}, {\"docid\": \"7927\", \"url\": \"https://www.imdb.com/list/ls072153898/\", \"title\": \"80's & 90's Authors\", \"title_span\": [11, 30], \"document_sha256\": \"dba8c853fef3fc3a56776bd0ab903ba6f15ed7e49f1fd2e936fb3d11506cc4e7\", \"window_ref\": \"w_177da5523f166cc0b3a3aa11\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: 80's & 90's Authors\\ndate: 2025-01-01\\n---\\nStephen Edwin King was born on September 21, 1947, at the Maine General Hospital in Portland. His parents were Nellie Ruth (Pillsbury), who worked as a caregiver at a mental institute, and Donald Edwin King, a merchant seaman. His father was born under the surname \\\"Pollock,\\\" but used the last name \\\"King,\\\" under which Stephen was born. He has an older brother, David. The Kings were a typical family until one night, when Donald said he was stepping out for cigarettes and was never heard from again. Ruth took over raising the family with help from relatives. They traveled throughout many states over several years, finally moving back to Durham, Maine, in 1958.\\n\\nStephen began his actual writing career in January of 1959, when David and Stephen decided to publish their own local newspaper named \\\"Dave's Rag\\\". David bought a mimeograph machine, and they put together a paper they sold for five cents an issue. Stephen attended Lisbon High School, in Lisbon, in 1962. Collaborating with his best friend Chris Chesley in 1963, they published a collection of 18 short stories called \\\"People, Places, and Things--Volume I\\\". King's stories included \\\"Hotel at the End of the Road\\\", \\\"I've Got to Get Away!\\\", \\\"The Dimension Warp\\\", \\\"The Thing at the Bottom of the Well\\\", \\\"The Stranger\\\", \\\"I'm Falling\\\", \\\"The Cursed Expedition\\\", and \\\"The Other Side of the Fog.\\\" A year later, King's amateur press, Triad and Gaslight Books, published a two-part book titled \\\"The Star Invaders\\\".\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1524, \"text_tokens\": 375, \"title_tokens\": 9, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.390977680683136}, {\"docid\": \"61397\", \"url\": \"https://www.onthisday.com/birthdays/date/1965/april\", \"title\": \"Famous People Born in April 1965\", \"title_span\": [11, 43], \"document_sha256\": \"edd2482312dcd3a2f9a7009de36d9937dbca62ae5616014ac6b7f14a062ba69a\", \"window_ref\": \"w_ab5e3c174ad832fb78312d56\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Famous People Born in April 1965\\ndate: 2025-01-01\\n---\\n- Apr 1 John \\\"Jumbo\\\" Elliott, American College Football HOF offensive tackle (Uni of Michigan; The Tunnel, a former warehouse where Biggie Smalls and Busta Rhymes once barked out raps to frenzied throngs, is converting to offices and luxury retail, blending seamlessly with the gleaming Hudson Yards to the north.\\n\\nAnd Gatien, with his icy demeanor and swashbuckler eye patch, is no longer the \\\"King of Clubs,\\\" as he was hailed by The New York Post in his '90s heyday. His spectacle megaclubs in the city — Limelight, Palladium, Club USA and the Tunnel — were raking in more than $1 million a week at the time, he said, before a drug trial, which he ultimately won, cost him, well, basically, everything.\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1405, \"text_tokens\": 358, \"title_tokens\": 17, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.3848554491996765}]"

King occasionally entertained the audience by telling amusing stories from his youth or early broadcasting career.\\n\\nWishing to reduce his workload, King began hosting a shorter, daytime version of the show in 1993. Jim Bohannon, King's primary fill-in host, took over the late night time slot. After 16 years on Mutual, King decided to retire from the program. The final broadcast of The Larry King Show was heard on May 27, 1994; Mutual gave King's afternoon slot to David Brenner and Mutual's affiliates were given the option of carrying the audio of King's new CNN evening television program. After Westwood One dissolved Mutual in 1999, the radio simulcast of the CNN show continued until December 31, 2009.\\n\\nLarry King Live\\n\\nLarry King Live began on CNN in June 1985. King hosted a broad range of guests, from figures such as UFO conspiracy theorists and alleged psychics,One notable guest was Sylvia Browne, who in 2005 told the Newsweek magazine that King, a believer in the paranormal, asks her to do private psychic readings. to prominent politicians and entertainment industry figures, often giving their first or only interview on breaking news stories on his show. In 1992, billionaire Ross Perot announced his presidential bid on the show. That gave me an enlightenment on life that \\\"don't get mad, get smart.\\\" That's why I want other kids to educate themselves, put it in their brain, they can't take that away.\\n\\nIn 1972 after serving three years and eleven months, King was released when his attorney got the conviction reduced to manslaughter. Accessed May 29, 2011.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nKing entered the boxing world after convincing Muhammad Ali to box in a charity exhibition for a local hospital in Cleveland with the help of singer Lloyd Price. Early on, he formed a partnership with a local promoter named Don Elbaum, who already had a stable of fighters in Cleveland and years of experience in boxing. In 1974, King negotiated to promote a heavyweight championship fight between Muhammad Ali and George Foreman in Zaire, popularly known as \\\"The Rumble in the Jungle\\\". The fight between Ali and Foreman was a much-anticipated event. King's family moved to Auckland for a while, where he attended Sacred Heart College, then returned to Wellington, where he attended St Patrick's College, Silverstream in Upper Hutt. His father Michael David Mwania, served in the Kenyan Army and his mother worked at the military hospital. At the age of six, he joined church productions at the Lang'ata Barracks. He completed his education from Lang'ata High School in Nairobi.\\n\\nHe is married to fellow actress Tess King.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nHe made acting debut in 2000 at the Kenya National Theatre for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanuka. He was a WMBM radio interviewer in the Miami area in the 1950s and 1960s and beginning in 1978, gained national prominence as host of The Larry King Show, an all-night nationwide call-in radio program heard over the Mutual Broadcasting System. From 1985 to 2010, he hosted the nightly interview television program Larry King Live on CNN. King hosted Larry King Now from 2012 to 2020, which aired on Hulu, Ora TV, and RT America. He hosted Politicking with Larry King, a weekly political talk show, on the same three channels from 2013 to 2020. King conducted over 50,000 interviews on radio and television.\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1243, \"text_tokens\": 366, \"title_tokens\": 4, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.49031272530555725}, {\"docid\": \"67431\", \"url\": \"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki\", \"title\": \"Peter Nzioki - Wikipedia\", \"title_span\": [11, 35], \"document_sha256\": \"df105e9610723015216b9cc93b7e7d9b84055f287422d1f577946fdb0b99d860\", \"window_ref\": \"w_847088d110a745604b5159e5\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Peter Nzioki - Wikipedia\\ndate: 2020-11-06\\n---\\nname: Peter King Nzioki Mwania\\nbirth_date: 25 May 1978\\nbirth_name: Peter King Nzioki Mwania\\nbirth_place: Kenya\\nnationality: Kenyan\\nheight: 1.8 m\\nyears_active: 2000–present\\nspouse: Tess King\\noccupation: Actor\\n\\nPeter King Nzioki Mwania (born 25 May 1978), popularly known as Peter King, is a Kenyan actor. He is best known for his roles in the films The Constant Gardener, The Fifth Estate and Sense8.\\n\\nPersonal life\\n\\nNzioki was born on 25 May 1978 in Nairobi, Kenya. His father Michael David Mwania, served in the Kenyan Army and his mother worked at the military hospital. At the age of six, he joined church productions at the Lang'ata Barracks. He completed his education from Lang'ata High School in Nairobi.\\n\\nHe is married to fellow actress Tess King.\\n\\nCareer\\n\\nHe made acting debut in 2000 at the Kenya National Theatre for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanuka. In theater, he played 'Iago' in the Phoenix Players production of the Shakespeare tragedy Othello. In 2005, he made his film debut with a minor role in The Constant Gardener directed by Fernando Meirelles. In the same year, he appeared as 'Barman' in the television movie Transit. He wrote or edited over 30 books on New Zealand topics, including the best-selling Penguin History of New Zealand, which was the most popular New Zealand book of 2004.\\n\\nLife\\n\\nKing was born in Wellington, one of four children to Eleanor and Lewis King, and grew up at Paremata. His Glasgow-born father was an advertising executive who had left New Zealand to serve as a naval officer in World War II and had risen to the rank of lieutenant-commander. King's family moved to Auckland for a while, where he attended Sacred Heart College, then returned to Wellington, where he attended St Patrick's College, Silverstream in Upper Hutt. King occasionally entertained the audience by telling amusing stories from his youth or early broadcasting career.\\n\\nWishing to reduce his workload, King began hosting a shorter, daytime version of the show in 1993. Jim Bohannon, King's primary fill-in host, took over the late night time slot. After 16 years on Mutual, King decided to retire from the program. The final broadcast of The Larry King Show was heard on May 27, 1994; Mutual gave King's afternoon slot to David Brenner and Mutual's affiliates were given the option of carrying the audio of King's new CNN evening television program. After Westwood One dissolved Mutual in 1999, the radio simulcast of the CNN show continued until December 31, 2009.\\n\\nLarry King Live\\n\\nLarry King Live began on CNN in June 1985. King hosted a broad range of guests, from figures such as UFO conspiracy theorists and alleged psychics,One notable guest was Sylvia Browne, who in 2005 told the Newsweek magazine that King, a believer in the paranormal, asks her to do private psychic readings. to prominent politicians and entertainment industry figures, often giving their first or only interview on breaking news stories on his show. He was a WMBM radio interviewer in the Miami area in the 1950s and 1960s and beginning in 1978, gained national prominence as host of The Larry King Show, an all-night nationwide call-in radio program heard over the Mutual Broadcasting System. His parents were Nellie Ruth (Pillsbury), who worked as a caregiver at a mental institute, and Donald Edwin King, a merchant seaman. His father was born under the surname \\\"Pollock,\\\" but used the last name \\\"King,\\\" under which Stephen was born. He has an older brother, David. The Kings were a typical family until one night, when Donald said he was stepping out for cigarettes and was never heard from again. Ruth took over raising the family with help from relatives. They traveled throughout many states over several years, finally moving back to Durham, Maine, in 1958.\\n\\nStephen began his actual writing career in January of 1959, when David and Stephen decided to publish their own local newspaper named \\\"Dave's Rag\\\". David bought a mimeograph machine, and they put together a paper they sold for five cents an issue. Stephen attended Lisbon High School, in Lisbon, in 1962. Collaborating with his best friend Chris Chesley in 1963, they published a collection of 18 short stories called \\\"People, Places, and Things--Volume I\\\". He studied history at Victoria University of Wellington, working part-time for the Evening Post, and graduated with a BA in 1967. \", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1476, \"text_tokens\": 384, \"title_tokens\": 8, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.40655717253685}, {\"docid\": \"78689\", \"url\": \"https://www.chicagotribune.com/2020/04/04/peter-gatien-the-90s-club-king-wants-his-final-say/\", \"title\": \"Peter Gatien, the '90s 'club king,' wants his final say\", \"title_span\": [11, 66], \"document_sha256\": \"6fc78ef0d0a0fafc1d5177aec08acc4536957b265b0e996efae65ba1f6d6d6bd\", \"window_ref\": \"w_1b0b58e2f036d722b7beff25\", \"text\": \"---\\ntitle: Peter Gatien, the '90s 'club king,' wants his final say\\nauthor: The New York Times\\ndate: 2020-04-04\\n---\\nNEW YORK — \\\"Thoughts flash in your mind of incredible nights here, whether it was Jay-Z, or Junior Vasquez, or the thousands of people inside and outside, waiting in line,\\\" said Peter Gatien, the nightclub impresario who lorded over the 1990s club scene in New York City.\\n\\nIt was a brisk Wednesday in early March, a few days before the city shut down because of the new coronavirus, and Gatien was at La Colombe, a cafe inside the brick warehouse that once housed the Tunnel, the massive nightclub on West 27th Street that is now celebrated as a crucible of hip-hop.\\n\\n\\\"Just the raw energy, the exuberance,\\\" he said, sipping an iced tea. \\\"You don't see it anymore.\\\"\\n\\nTimes change. The Tunnel, a former warehouse where Biggie Smalls and Busta Rhymes once barked out raps to frenzied throngs, is converting to offices and luxury retail, blending seamlessly with the gleaming Hudson Yards to the north.\\n\\nAnd Gatien, with his icy demeanor and swashbuckler eye patch, is no longer the \\\"King of Clubs,\\\" as he was hailed by The New York Post in his '90s heyday. His spectacle megaclubs in the city — Limelight, Palladium, Club USA and the Tunnel — were raking in more than $1 million a week at the time, he said, before a drug trial, which he ultimately won, cost him, well, basically, everything.\\n\", \"offset\": 0, \"end_char\": 1405, \"text_tokens\": 358, \"title_tokens\": 17, \"has_more_before\": false, \"has_more_after\": true, \"parent_window_ref\": null, \"status\": \"ok\", \"score\": 0.3848554491996765}]"
